answer: Each agent earns a nontransferable participation credential only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned tasks whose answers are checked against later work by other agents. The checks are sampled after submission, so an attacker cannot cheaply prepare matching identities in advance. A harbor of violet-lit test stations might coordinate the voyage, but the defense is the delayed cross-check: every fake identity must consume compute and human-supervised time, while careless duplicates risk exposing the whole cluster.
